A brief video about Noriaki Inoue, Morihei's nephew

Well, I figured I would help get us started over here by sharing a video of a historical nature.

Inoue was Morihei Ueshiba's nephew and was present during a lot of his training with Sokaku Takeda. For many years they were very close and Inoue served as Morihei's "right hand man," traveling to teach as his representative. He was really influential in the pre-war years in what would become aikido, not to mention received instruction from Sokaku himself and as I said, having extensive one-on-one time with Morihei.

I hope others enjoy a little glimpse into the past of someone who's not usually mentioned. Although the video of him doing technique is very late in his life, I think it'll be readily apparent to anyone familiar with aikido just how similar Inoue's "Shin'ei Taido" (also called aiki-budo before) is to Morihei's aikido, especially as you see it in pre-war variants.
He is really the only person who turned out anything like Ueshiba. No clue if that is a good thing or not.

The historian in me would love to see footage of Inoue from his younger years, similar to the 1935 video of Ueshiba. I'd imagine other footage of him exists, maybe even stuff from before the '80s, though given Inoue's paranoia and the secretive nature of Daito Ryu people in general anything like that will probably stay squirreled away until the owner dies and it ends up in some Japanese recycling plant.

I think it's probably a good thing they seem similar, at least in terms of jujutsu, because it helps me see closer to Takeda's Daito Ryu. Of course it helps none with the important stuff we really just can't see from a video.. but as you know I'm kind of a nerd and enjoy this old aikido/DR history stuff.
